name: Migration catalog
purpose: The in-tree source of schema truth. An ordered list of migration entries, each carrying a monotonic version integer, a human description string, and one or more DDL/data statements. The catalog lives next to the store facade and is imported by the migration runner at open. Its max version is the build's max known migration version, which the refuse-newer comparison and the schemaVersion read both anchor against.
responsibilities: Expose an ordered sequence of migration entries starting at version 1 with no gaps; each entry has fields { version, description, statements } where statements is a non-empty list of engine-native DDL/data statements (AC-5102-1).
Expose the max version integer as a named export the store facade reads for schemaVersion contract validation and refuse-newer comparison (AC-5102-2).
Hold every schema change ever shipped in this project's history; a schema change that is not a new numbered entry in this catalog is not a shipped schema change (AC-5102-1).
internalStructure: One source-tree module exporting MIGRATIONS (the ordered array) and CURRENT_VERSION (the max version integer). Entries are appended, never edited: a shipped migration is a fact of production and any correction is a new migration that supersedes it. The statements field's dialect matches the engine ADR-601 selected; SQLite dialect at v1.0.0 unless a project supersedes ADR-601.

interfaces.name: MIGRATIONS
interfaces.description: The ordered array of { version, description, statements } entries, exported as a named module-level constant.

interfaces.name: CURRENT_VERSION
interfaces.description: The max version integer across MIGRATIONS. Equals MIGRATIONS[MIGRATIONS.length - 1].version by construction.

tradeoffs: One central catalog file is trivial to reason about at small history (up to a few dozen entries) and starts to strain review at large history. Projects that outgrow one file split into one-file-per-migration under a directory the module aggregates, preserving the exported MIGRATIONS shape. Statements-as-strings keeps the catalog readable but couples it to one engine dialect; supporting two engines from one catalog requires a per-entry dialect indirection the v1.0.0 shape does not carry and the blueprint does not recommend before a project needs it.
